snes9x.verified_with: node tools/run-smoke.mjs cores/snes9x_libretro.js 60 — ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED, ~1.1 ms/frame, no ASYNCIFY. See cores/snes9x.json.

makefile_edits: The upstream emscripten platform block emitted only an intermediate LLVM bitcode archive (.bc). It performs the full Emscripten link to <profile>.js + .wasm with CC=emcc/CXX=em++/LD=em++, STATIC_LINKING=0, and the raw-libretro flag set (ALLOW_TABLE_GROWTH, exported runtime methods incl. addFunction, exported retro_*). This follow-up added: (1) -s ASYNCIFY=1 -s ASYNCIFY_STACK_SIZE=1048576 so retro_run yields to the browser and returns instead of hanging in bsnes's libco scheduler; (2) per-PROFILE DISTINCT output filename + MODULARIZE EXPORT_NAME (bsnes_accuracy / bsnes_performance) so both cores can coexist without a symbol collision; (3) -s EXPORT_ES6=1 so each core is an ES6 default-export factory that core-loader.js resolves via dynamic import.
libco_backend_edit: libco defaults to the sjlj (setjmp/longjmp) backend under Emscripten, whose raw-stack context switches ASYNCIFY cannot unwind (retro_run hang). Added libco/emscripten.c, an Emscripten Fibers (emscripten_fiber_*) libco backend, and wired it in libco/libco.c under the __EMSCRIPTEN__ target so cothread switches cooperate with ASYNCIFY.
verified_with: node tools/run-smoke.mjs cores/<profile>.js 12 — for BOTH profiles: retro_load_game()==true, retro_run() RETURNS within a bounded wall clock (no hang), video_refresh fires with a non-null framebuffer, and the frame counter advances across the run. Note: the harness re-execs Node with --liftoff-only to avoid a Node/V8 TurboFan codegen crash (IdField::is_valid) when JIT-optimizing these large ASYNCIFY WASM modules — a Node-side JIT limit, not a core defect (browsers do not hit it).

noasyncify_experiment.goal: Test whether bsnes-mercury accuracy can run WITHOUT ASYNCIFY (a smaller, faster core) inside a Web Worker, since a worker thread blocking is acceptable (it does not freeze the UI). The user specifically asked to try -s SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm and native fiber switching for libco cothreads.
flags_tried: kept: -s ALLOW_TABLE_GROWTH=1, -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1, -s INITIAL_MEMORY=134217728, -s STACK_SIZE=8388608, -s MODULARIZE=1, -s EXPORT_ES6=1, -s EXPORT_NAME=bsnes_accuracy_noasyncify, -s ENVIRONMENT=web,worker,node, single-threaded (no pthreads), same 22 retro_* exports (no retro_cheat_*)
noasyncify_experiment.output_names: bsnes_mercury_accuracy_libretro_noasyncify.{js,wasm} (EXPORT_NAME bsnes_accuracy_noasyncify) — built to a scratch dir OUTSIDE the repo, never committed.
noasyncify_experiment.libco_backend_tried: The Emscripten Fibers backend (libco/emscripten.c) is implemented ON TOP OF Asyncify (emscripten_fiber_* require -s ASYNCIFY), so it cannot be used in a no-ASYNCIFY build. libco.c was taught to fall back to the sjlj (setjmp/longjmp) backend under __EMSCRIPTEN__ when LIBCO_NO_ASYNCIFY is defined, relying on -s SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm so longjmp uses Wasm exception handling. (Makefile NOASYNCIFY=1 variant + libco/libco.c LIBCO_NO_ASYNCIFY guard, both in the /projects/bsnes-mercury source tree, additive + gated so the shipping ASYNCIFY build is unchanged.)
noasyncify_experiment.build_result: COMPILED + LINKED cleanly. .wasm was ~1.6 MB (vs ~3.7 MB for the ASYNCIFY build — confirming no ASYNCIFY instrumentation). Loaded fine: retro_load_game()==true, av_info 256x224 @ 60.099 fps, WRAM ptr+size present.
noasyncify_experiment.run_smoke_result: HUNG/THREW — FAIL. `node tools/run-smoke.mjs <scratch>/bsnes_mercury_accuracy_libretro_noasyncify.js 12` (RUN_TIMEOUT_MS=20000): the very FIRST retro_run() threw a WebAssembly.Exception (message undefined) immediately — 0 frames advanced, 0 video_refresh calls. Root cause: libco's sjlj backend swaps cothreads via sigaltstack/raise(SIGUSR1)/sigsetjmp/siglongjmp, which do not perform a real stack switch under WASM; SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm only rewrites C longjmp into a Wasm-EH throw, so the cothread 'switch' unwinds as an exception out of retro_run instead of transferring control to the CPU/PPU cothread. This is the same class of failure (libco cannot switch raw stacks under WASM) that originally forced ASYNCIFY + Emscripten Fibers.
noasyncify_experiment.decision: FELL BACK. Did NOT ship a no-ASYNCIFY bsnes core. snes9x-in-a-worker (synchronous, no ASYNCIFY, delivered by FEAT-002) remains the real-time default and already fixes the user's iOS main-thread problem; the two existing ASYNCIFY bsnes cores remain for paused frame-perfect work. No new core, catalog entry, sw.js entry, or build detritus was added. All three shipping cores still pass run-smoke after the experiment.
noasyncify_experiment.conclusion: A no-ASYNCIFY bsnes-accuracy core is NOT viable with the available libco backends: emscripten fibers require ASYNCIFY, and sjlj cannot swap cothreads under WASM even with SUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm/-fwasm-exceptions. ASYNCIFY + Emscripten Fibers remains the only working configuration for bsnes. This confirms the migration does not depend on this experiment.
